Medium Affected: WATER

Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 25 gallons
HYDRAULIC OIL DISCHARGED TO A LINE RETENTION POND FROM A HEAT EXCHANGER. MUCH OF THE RELEASE WAS CONTAINED IN THE POND, BUT A SLIGHT SHEEN WAS OBSERVED AT THE OUTFALL AT THE MUSKEGON RIVER. THE SOURCE HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED AND ISOLATED. ACCORDING TO THE MDSM, THE MATERIAL IS INHERENTLY BIODEGRADABLE, NOT HARMFUL TO AQUATIC ORGANISMS, AND RCRA NON-HAZADROUS. THE RELEASE WAS CONFINED WITH BOOMS AND REMOVED USING SUITABLE ABSORBENTS CONSISTENT WITH THE MSDS. ALL HYDRAULIC PRESSES WERE TESTED FOR LEAK DETECTION. A SAMPLE OF THE RETENTION POND WATER WAS ANALYZED AND POSITIVELY IDENTIFIED AS HYDRAULIC OIL. NO OTHER CONSTITUENTS WERE FOUND IN THE EPA-CERTIFIED ANALYSIS. AFFECTED WATER FROM THE POND WAS PUMPED OUT AND HAULED OFF SITE FOR TREATMENT/DISPOSAL.

properties.content:

Nearest City: Derby Line, VT
Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: OIL: DIESEL
Medium Affected: SOIL
Suspected Responsible Party: FRED'S PLUMBING & HEATING INC.
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 100 gallons
UPON ARRIVAL AT CUSTOMER'S FARM, FUEL DELIVERY DRIVER PRESET DIGITAL METER FOR DELIVERY OF 100 GALLONS OF OFFROAD DIESEL IN CUSTOMER'S 300 GALLON AST. DRIVER COMMENCED DISPENSING OPERATION, THEN WALKED AWAY FROM THE NOZZLE TO SPEAK WITH THE CUSTOMER IN THE BARN. CUSTOMER'S WIFE ALERTED DRIVER THAT FUEL WAS RUNNING ON THE GROUND. DRIVER RAN TO TANK TRUCK, STOPPED PUMP, THEN IMMEDIATELY STARTED SPILL RESPONSE PROCEDURES SETTING OUT ABSORBENT PADS AND A BOOM TO CONTAIN THE SPILL TO MINIMIZE THE SPREAD OF FUEL. HE THEN CALLED DISPATCH WHO INITIATED RESPONSE FOR A SPILL CLEAN UP, AND THEN HE RETURNED TO SPILL CONTAINMENT UNTIL HELP ARRIVED. CONTRACTOR RESPONDED WITH EQUIPMENT INCLUDING A VAC TRAILER TO CAPTURE POOLED FREE PRODUCT. A SECOND CONTRACTOR, ALSO CALLED TO RESPOND, TESTED AND OVERSAW THE REMOVAL OF DIESEL FUEL CONTAMINATED SOILS.
